Open questions: whether this project's DuckDB-only stack is the right target for a documentation database or whether it should be the same store the vector/graph retrieval ideas land on; whether front-matter review should happen before or alongside schema changes already implied by open plans (e.g. PLAN-017's idea/plan lifecycle work); and how a documentation database stays in sync with hand-edited markdown without becoming another thing that drifts, the way docs/08-governance/catalog.md already has a generated-vs-committed staleness check today.

title: Explore graph database tooling for a documentation & knowledge database, distinct from the existing GitNexus code-graph idea
body:
Idea 000005 already covers graph-based retrieval for code structure specifically — GitNexus/KuzuDB parsing a repository into functions/classes/imports with Cypher queries, framed there as complementary to vector search ("graph RAG answers questions about code structure, vector search answers questions about knowledge memories"). This idea is the other half of that same question: what graph database tooling would fit a documentation and knowledge database, not a code-structure graph.

The repository's documents already form a real graph today, just not one anything can query as one: depends_on edges between plans/requirements/sessions in front matter, promoted_to links from ideas to plans, systems arrays connecting documents to docs/08-governance/systems.yaml components, and (per the idea priority queue and backlog next_up mechanisms already built) explicit ordering relationships. A graph database purpose-built for this — decisions, sessions, plans, requirements, ideas, and their cross-references — could answer questions like "what led to this decision" or "what session history touches this system" by traversal instead of by an agent manually following links across docs/03-sessions, docs/04-decisions and docs/01-plans.

The idea is specifically to survey what's available for this use case (embedded options like KuzuDB — already surfaced by 000005 for a different purpose — versus a hosted/server graph DB like Neo4j, versus something lighter-weight given this project's existing DuckDB-only, no-server-dependency stack) and evaluate fit, not to build anything yet. Open questions: whether one graph database should serve both this and the code-structure use case from 000005, or whether documentation/knowledge graphing and code graphing are different enough problems to warrant separate tools; how a documentation graph would be kept in sync with hand-edited markdown front matter without drifting (the same sync concern raised in the companion "documentation database for knowledge retrieval" idea); and whether this is even the right retrieval mechanism versus the vector DB approach being explored in the companion idea recorded alongside this one, or whether — as 000005 suggests for the code case — the two turn out to be complementary rather than either/or here too.

title: Explore vector database tooling for a knowledge retrieval system
body:
Companion to the ideas recorded alongside this one about reviewing documentation front matter for a documentation database, and about graph database tooling for that same documentation/knowledge corpus. Where those explore structured/relational and graph retrieval respectively, this idea is about semantic retrieval: what vector database options fit a knowledge retrieval system over this repository's documentation, session history, decisions and memories.

Context already in the backlog: the phase-mem-* line (phase-mem-01 through at least phase-mem-06, plan doc-agent-memory) implements an agent memory system that is explicitly vector-based per idea 000005's framing ("the whole phase-mem-* line is vector-based"), and idea 000020 (MCP-mediated multi-agent coordination with a Librarian context service) separately proposes "a vector database behind the MCP server, holding indexed context (decisions, session history, plan/requirement content) so agents can query semantically instead of grepping/reading whole files." Neither of those ideas has evaluated specific vector DB tooling — this idea is that evaluation: surveying embedded/local options (e.g. something that fits alongside the existing DuckDB-only, no-server-dependency stack — DuckDB itself has a vector similarity extension worth checking) versus hosted/server options, and what tradeoffs matter here (ingestion story for markdown + JSONL sources, embedding model choice, how updates/deletes are handled as documents change, query latency for an agent mid-session).

Open questions: whether this should target the existing phase-mem-* memory system specifically, the broader documentation/knowledge retrieval use case from this idea's two companions, both, or informs a design decision between them; whether DuckDB's own vector capabilities make a separate vector database unnecessary here (consistent with this project's preference for one embedded store rather than accumulating KuzuDB-for-graph plus something-else-for-vectors plus DuckDB); and how this relates to 000005's stated complementary framing (graph for structure, vector for semantic/knowledge) — whether that framing holds once concrete tools are evaluated rather than assumed.

title: An idea planner agent that turns a promoted idea into a governed plan
body:
An agent that takes an idea already past triage — ideally one the owner has moved to
reviewing or is about to promote — and drafts the governed `plan` document (and, where the
idea implies observable behavior, the paired `requirement` document) that AGENTS.md requires
before implementation code is written. Today that drafting is entirely manual: the owner or
an ad-hoc session writes the plan by hand, working from the idea's title, body and whatever
triage findings and links exist on it.

The natural boundary mirrors the triage agent's: it drafts, it does not decide. It should
produce a plan document sized and shaped like the existing ones in docs/01-plans/ (context
and scope, decisions with rejected alternatives and their real costs, deliverables,
sequencing), pull in what triage already found (related plans, phases, overlapping ideas) so
the draft does not duplicate coverage the triage pass already surfaced, and allocate its
document code the normal way (`--next-code plan`). It should not itself promote the idea —
that status transition, and confirming the draft is good enough to become the real plan,
stays the owner's call, the same way triage stops at `triaged` rather than deciding
`promoted`.

This is where the second idea (auditing what makes a plan qualitatively good) becomes a
prerequisite rather than a nice-to-have: an agent drafting plans needs a concrete rubric to
draft toward, not just "look like the existing ones." Until that audit exists, this agent has
no target to aim for beyond mimicry of whichever plan it happened to read first.

Open questions: does it draft into `_working/` for the owner to promote to a coded document,
or does it allocate the code itself and write directly into `docs/01-plans/`? Given
`_working/`'s definition (ephemeral, deleted rather than rewritten once the task finishes)
this plan is not ephemeral — it is meant to become the permanent document — so a `_working/`
staging step feels like the wrong shape, but writing straight into governed `docs/` without
owner review before a code is spent also feels premature. Worth resolving during triage or
before scoping a phase.

title: Audit what makes a plan document qualitatively good: structure, style, tone, format
body:
docs/01-plans/ has around two dozen plans by now, written across many sessions, and they are
not uniform. Some (PLAN-016, PLAN-017 and its children) are dense with rejected alternatives,
their real costs, and explicit owner-quoted decisions. Others are thinner — a scope list and
a deliverables list with little explanation of why the shape was chosen over another. Nothing
currently states what distinguishes the two, so every new plan is written by pattern-matching
against whichever existing plan the author happened to have open, and drift compounds with
each session.

The audit should look across the existing plan corpus and name, concretely: what structural
sections a good plan actually has (and which of the ones in use — context and scope,
decisions, deliverables, sequencing, open questions — earn their place versus which are
cargo-culted); what tone and voice work (first-person owner quotes vs. third-person
description; how much hedging is appropriate on an unconfirmed judgment call vs. a settled
decision); how much justification a decision needs before it's traceable six months later
without reconstructing the conversation that produced it; and what "too long" or "too thin"
actually look like in a real example from the corpus, not in the abstract.

This is explicitly a prerequisite for the idea-planner-agent idea recorded alongside this
one: an agent drafting plans needs a rubric, and "read some existing plans and imitate them"
is not a rubric, it's the same drift-by-pattern-matching problem this audit exists to fix.
It may also be useful on its own — as a checklist the owner or a reviewing agent runs against
any plan before it leaves draft status, independent of whether the planner agent ever gets
built.

Scope note: this is an audit and a written standard, not a rewrite of every existing plan to
match it. Whether existing plans get retrofitted, grandfathered, or left alone once the
standard exists is a separate decision.

author: agent-idea-triage
text:
Overlap with idea 000047 ("Audit what makes a plan document qualitatively good") is explicit and mutual: 000047's own body names 000046 directly ("the idea-planner-agent idea recorded alongside this one") and calls itself a prerequisite for it; 000046's body makes the same claim from the other side ("This is where the second idea ... becomes a prerequisite rather than a nice-to-have"). No `linked` event exists yet on either idea despite the two-way textual cross-reference.

This idea explicitly models its own boundary on idea 000007 ("An agent for triaging parked ideas" - the source of the triage agent that produced this finding): "The natural boundary mirrors the triage agent's: it drafts, it does not decide." 000007 is the origin of the drafts-not-decides pattern this idea proposes to extend to plan authoring.

Idea 000038 ("Formalize the requirements-vs-plans process and design") is closely related but not identical: 000038 wants the *rule* for when a paired requirement document is mandatory versus when a plan's acceptance section suffices, and notes only 1 of 18+ plans is a clean paired example. 000046 assumes an agent would draft "the paired requirement document, where the idea implies observable behavior" - i.e. it presupposes a decision rule that, per 000038, does not currently exist in written form. An idea-planner agent would need 000038's outcome (or would independently reinvent the same judgment call) to know when to draft a requirement alongside the plan.

Governed documents found relevant to the idea's own "open questions" section (where to stage the draft):
- PLAN-015-ephemeral-working-plans.md defines `_working/` as ephemeral task detail for a phase that already exists, deleted rather than rewritten when the task finishes - which is why 000046 itself observes a `_working/` staging step "feels like the wrong shape" for a document meant to become permanent.
- ADR-010-idea-staging.md (`docs/00-working/`) is adjacent but describes idea staging, not plan/requirement staging, and explicitly says an idea "ends in a status - promoted into a plan, requirement or phase" without specifying the mechanics of that promotion, which is the exact gap 000046 is pointing at.
- REQ-004-plans-directory-consolidation.md documents the current canonical single location for governed plans (`docs/01-plans/`) but has no bearing on pre-promotion staging.

No existing backlog phase covers this ground: the `phase-idea-*` track (phase-idea-01 through phase-idea-09) built the ideas-log infrastructure itself (writer, fold projection, annotations, linked events) and phase-idea-02 is the triage agent this idea mirrors: no phase for drafting a plan/requirement from a promoted idea exists yet.

author: agent-idea-triage
text:
Explicit cross-reference to idea 000046: 000047's own body says the audit is "explicitly a prerequisite for the idea-planner-agent idea recorded alongside this one," and 000046's body (read in full) reciprocally names 000047 as "the second idea (auditing what [makes a plan good])." Both bodies point at each other by description; neither idea currently carries a `linked` event.

Topical overlap with idea 000038 ("Formalize the requirements-vs-plans process and design"): 000038 asks when a standalone requirement document is mandatory versus when a plan's own acceptance section suffices, and what belongs in a requirement versus a plan. 000047 asks a narrower, different-axis question — given a plan document, what structural sections, tone, and justification depth make it qualitatively good. Different questions (doc-kind boundary vs. within-plan quality) but both are about formalizing plan-document contract/shape and read naturally as adjacent work.

Existing governance material found: templates/governance/document.md is the only generic template covering plan structure today — it defines four generic sections (Context and scope; Work and dependencies; Acceptance and verification; Open questions) shared across all document kinds (plan, ADR, requirement, etc.), with no plan-specific guidance on tone, hedging, or justification depth. No existing ADR, requirement, or plan was found that names a rubric or checklist for plan quality specifically — grep of docs/01-plans/, docs/06-requirements/, docs/04-decisions/ and docs/09-backlog/backlog.yaml for terms like "rubric", "plan quality", "good plan" and "audit" (in the sense this idea uses it) turned up no matching document. REQ-003 (doc-idea-plan-lifecycle-requirements) and REQ-004 (plans-directory-consolidation) both touch the plan corpus but address lifecycle/location integrity, not document quality.

No related backlog.yaml phase found addressing plan-document quality/style specifically.

title: An idea scribe agent: a dedicated writer that appends ideas so capture never spends main-session context
body:
Recording an idea today happens inline in whatever session the thought came up in: the main
session drafts title and body, writes them to a temp file, and calls
`tools/append_idea.py add --file`, per `.claude/commands/idea.md`. That's cheap for one idea,
but every idea recorded this way spends main-session context on drafting prose that, once
written, the main session never needs to see again — and a session capturing several ideas in
a row (as this one just did, for 000046 and 000047) pays that cost repeatedly.

The proposed agent is a pure writer, mirroring `idea-triage`'s split of "the driver decides
when to invoke, the subagent does the one bounded task": given raw prose (however rough — a
sentence, a half-formed thought, a paste from elsewhere), it distills the title and body per
`idea.md`'s existing guidance ("what the idea is, why it came up, what it would touch, what is
unresolved") and calls `append_idea.py add --file`, using the same file-based-input safety
rule idea-triage already follows for its own writes (never inline prose into a shell
argument — idea 000019's corruption is the standing cautionary example). It reports back the
assigned id and title, not the full body, keeping the round-trip cheap for the caller.

This is a narrower, cheaper counterpart to `idea-triage`, not a competitor to it: this agent
only ever calls `add` (never `annotate`, `status`, `link` or anything else), and it runs at
capture time, before triage ever sees the idea. Same rationale as `phase-idea-01`'s writer
being deterministic tooling — the scribe's job is formatting prose into the sanctioned shape
without judgment, not deciding whether the idea is worth recording. `ADR-010`'s "capture as
given, never filtered at entry" applies here exactly as it does to `idea.md` today: the scribe
records what it's given, it does not decline or merge it into something existing.

Open question: is this worth its own subagent given how cheap the existing `idea.md` command
already is, or does the actual cost belong to whoever is drafting the title/body prose in the
first place — cheapening the round-trip doesn't remove that cost, it just moves it to a model
running at a lower tier (haiku, per idea-triage's precedent). Worth weighing against just
tightening `idea.md`'s own guidance during triage of this idea.

title: Define where a promoted plan or requirement document lives before it earns a code
body:
An idea's status machine ends at `promoted` — "became a plan, requirement or phase" — but
nothing governed actually says what happens between "the owner decided this idea should
become a plan" and "the plan exists as a coded document in docs/01-plans/". `ADR-010` covers
idea staging (`docs/00-working/`) but explicitly stops at promotion without describing the
mechanics of it. `PLAN-015` defines `_working/` as ephemeral task detail for a phase that
already exists — deleted rather than rewritten once the task finishes — which is the wrong
shape for a document meant to become permanent, not disposable, once written.

This gap surfaced concretely during triage of idea 000046 (an idea-planner agent that would
draft governed plans from promoted ideas): both its own body and the idea-triage agent's
finding on it flagged the same open question — does a drafted plan get written straight into
`docs/01-plans/` with a code allocated up front, or does it stage somewhere first for owner
review before a code is spent? Right now this question has no answer even for a human doing
the promotion by hand; it only became visible because an agent doing it mechanically forced
the question to be asked explicitly.

The idea is to define that staging step (or explicitly decide there isn't one and a promoted
document goes straight to a coded file, reviewed in place). Whatever the answer, it should
cover both the manual case (the owner promoting an idea themselves) and the agentic case (a
future idea-planner-agent, 000046, doing the drafting) with the same rule — not one process
for humans and a different one for agents.

author: agent-idea-triage
text:
No idea currently proposes a scribe/capture-writer agent, and no backlog phase covers this ground: phase-idea-01 (complete) and phase-idea-02 (active, the triage agent) are the only phase-idea-* entries touching agent-mediated writes to _data/ideas.jsonl, and phase-idea-02's scope is triage (finding annotations, open-to-triaged), not capture (add).

Idea 000007 ("An agent for triaging parked ideas") is this idea's own stated model for the driver/subagent split ("mirroring idea-triage's split of 'the driver decides when to invoke, the subagent does the one bounded task'"). 000048 proposes extending that same split one step earlier in the lifecycle — capture instead of triage — rather than overlapping 000007's ground; the two are complementary, not competing, and 000048's body already frames it that way ("narrower, cheaper counterpart to idea-triage, not a competitor").

phase-idea-01's own scope (backlog.yaml) already delivered the mechanism this idea would use: "Write tools/append_idea.py, which takes prose and generates the id, timestamp and event; it is the only sanctioned writer" plus "Expose it as a custom tool an agent can call, wrapping the script rather than reimplementing it." So the tool-wrapper precedent for an agent calling append_idea.py already exists and shipped; this idea would be a new agent definition built on top of already-delivered infrastructure, not new tooling.

.claude/commands/idea.md is the document this idea would most directly sit beside or replace: it currently carries the exact guidance ("what the idea is, why it came up, what it would touch, what is unresolved"), the same file-based-input safety rule citing idea 000019's corruption, and the same "record as given, never filtered at entry" framing this idea's body cites from ADR-010. If built, the scribe agent would be doing mechanically what idea.md's command instructs a session to do by hand today — the idea's own "Worth weighing against just tightening idea.md's own guidance" open question is accurate: idea.md is the artifact in direct tension with building a new agent, not a separate concern.

ADR-010's "Ideas are recorded as given, not filtered at entry" section is the passage the idea cites correctly; it says overlap is noted inside the entry and left for triage, which matches the idea's own claim that the scribe "does not decline or merge it into something existing."

Checked idea 000049 (define where a promoted plan/requirement document lives before it earns a code, created after 000048) for overlap: it addresses the opposite end of the lifecycle — staging a promoted plan/requirement document, not capturing a new idea at intake — and does not overlap 000048's ground beyond both concerning writer-agent boundaries in the idea/plan pipeline.

No PROPOSED LINK: the relationships found (000007, phase-idea-01, idea.md) are structural precedent and a possible document to amend, not idea-to-idea overlap warranting a typed edge.

author: agent-claude
text:
Backfilled promotion: this idea's content is delivered specifically as phase-idea-02 (build
the idea triage agent) under PLAN-016 (idea record system). promoted_to names PLAN-016
because promotion targets are governed document codes, not backlog phase ids, but the
implementing unit is the phase, not the whole plan. Backfilled on 2026-09-08 because the idea
and the plan/phase covering it were created in the same session as the idea itself, before
this promotion step was applied — status went straight from open to phase-idea-02 being
built and shipped without the idea's own record being updated to match.

author: agent-idea-triage
text:
Idea 000003 asks for a skill that updates session records mid-session, invocable by the owner or agent when either sees value, with an open question about whether the model should invoke it unprompted or only offer. This work is already fully delivered.

Phase-ses-03 ("Build the checkpoint skill", PLAN-008) is marked complete in backlog.yaml. The checkpoint skill exists at `.claude/skills/checkpoint/SKILL.md` and:
- Records what has happened mid-session at natural pauses (step 1, 3, 5 of its own procedure; step 9 reports honestly on idempotency)
- Is invocable by either owner or agent any number of times (SKILL.md step 1 explicitly permits agent invocation; PLAN-008 phase 3 states "a skill can be invoked by either party")
- Clarifies the answer to the open question: agent should invoke it unprompted when "it notices a lot has happened since the last one", not merely offer (PLAN-008 line 121–123: "an agent that does not know the skill exists will not choose to run it", implying agents do choose to run it when they know)
- Records verification output, session record with allocated code, backlog status and evidence, next_up pruning, and catalog regeneration, leaving the tree honest and never claiming completion that is not there

This idea's actual deliverable is live and in production.

author: agent-idea-triage
text:
Idea 000001 asks a strategic question about fixture governance for the HTML generation system once PLAN-003 is built: where fixtures live (generated from `_data/` vs hand-authored), whether they count as governed artifacts or test assets, and how schema changes invalidate them.

The HTML generation plan (`PLAN-003`, approved but not built) includes six backlog phases (`phase-html-01` through `phase-html-10`), and several already specify fixture testing at component level:

- `phase-html-02` includes temporary-tree, invalid-input and stale-output tests (`test/test_build_pages.py`)
- `phase-html-03` uses "contract fixtures" to verify alignment with JSON Schemas (`test/test_page_models.py`)
- `phase-html-04` runs "TestClient tests with temporary page files" for success, missing, traversal and invalid cases (`test/test_pages_api.py`)
- `phase-html-07` renders "representative optional-field and long-text fixtures" in verification

These phase-level fixtures are component-specific (schema validator, API responses, component rendering). Idea 000001 is asking the meta-question: what is the system-wide governance and storage strategy across all HTML fixtures, and when does schema change break the fixture suite?

This is a prerequisite design question, not yet covered by the phases' tactical fixture decisions. The phases will generate temporary test artifacts; 000001 is asking whether a durable fixture catalog should exist, where it lives if it does, and whether the audit scans `test/` at all (currently it does not per PLAN-010's deliverables).

Overlaps with 000035 (Contract compiler and mutation-driven fixture suite from JSON Schema), which extends the concept to generated, mutation-driven fixtures across the entire system schema library — a higher-level question that presumes a fixture strategy exists.

No related plan, requirement or governance document found that specifies HTML fixture strategy.

author: agent-idea-triage
text:
Idea 000003 asks for a skill that updates session records mid-session, invocable by the owner or agent when either sees value, with an open question about whether the model should invoke it unprompted or only offer. This work is already fully delivered.

Phase-ses-03 ("Build the checkpoint skill", PLAN-008) is marked complete in backlog.yaml. The checkpoint skill exists at `.claude/skills/checkpoint/SKILL.md` and:
- Records what has happened mid-session at natural pauses (step 1, 3, 5 of its own procedure; step 9 reports honestly on idempotency)
- Is invocable by either owner or agent any number of times (SKILL.md step 1 explicitly permits agent invocation; PLAN-008 phase 3 states "a skill can be invoked by either party")

- Records verification output, session record with allocated code, backlog status and evidence, next_up pruning, and catalog regeneration, leaving the tree honest and never claiming completion that is not there

This idea's actual deliverable is live and in production.

PROPOSED PROMOTION: 000003 -> PLAN-008 (The checkpoint skill, phase-ses-03 of PLAN-008, is the exact deliverable: a skill for mid-session session-record updates, safe to invoke unprompted by agents or the owner, now complete and deployed)

author: agent-idea-triage
text:
## Finding for Idea 000002: Prioritised search order for agentic knowledge retrieval

Idea 000002 asks for a **stated ordering of sources** when agents answer "how does X work?" or "why was X chosen?" — addressing how to sequence consultation of code, plans, ADRs, session records, and ideas list when those sources disagree predictably (code is what exists, plans are intent, ADRs are why, sessions are what happened, ideas are speculation).

**Related existing plan:** PLAN-001 (Agent Memory System) defines The Librarian as a retrieval router with a layered pipeline: exact-ID lookup → tag filter → keyword/FTS → semantic/vector → agentic refinement. It also specifies that results be ranked and returned with confidence levels and retrieval method metadata. However, PLAN-001's layers address **retrieval mechanics** (method and cost efficiency), not **source priority** (which document type to consult first when answering a specific question type). These are complementary: source ordering rules could be implemented within The Librarian's retrieval contract or agentic refinement loop, but PLAN-001 does not yet specify them.

**Related backlog phases:** phase-mem-07 (implement nonsemantic Librarian retrieval contract with confidence/recency metadata), phase-mem-08 (specify retrieval-hint contract), and phase-mem-09 (implement blended hints) are building out The Librarian with machinery for scoring and routing, but again address mechanics, not source priority ordering.

**Related idea overlap:** 000020 (MCP-mediated Librarian context service) proposes infrastructure for mediated context retrieval and a Librarian agent that could implement prioritization, but is broader and does not specifically address source ordering or the "confidence/freshness signal" for disagreement resolution that 000002 raises.

**No conflicting decisions found.** ADR-012 discusses sources of truth (git vs. session records) but in the context of system design, not in the context of agentic retrieval order.

**Specific open questions from 000002 that remain unresolved:**
- Does source order vary by question type ("how" vs. "why")?
- Should sources carry confidence/freshness signals for weighing disagreement?
- What resolves genuine conflict between sources (e.g., code vs. newer ADR)?
- Should this rule live in `tools/load_context.py`, `AGENTS.md`, or both?

The idea is a **design question orthogonal to PLAN-001**, not a duplicate of it: both addressing the retrieval system, but one specifying **mechanics** and the other specifying **source priority semantics**.

author: agent-idea-triage
text:
## Triage finding: 000005 (Graph databases and GitNexus)

**Overlap with other ideas:** 
- 000044 (Explore graph database tooling for documentation/knowledge) explicitly addresses the documentation-side graph retrieval gap, positioned as distinct from 000005's code-structure focus (GitNexus/KuzuDB for code). Both frame graph and vector approaches as complementary rather than competing.
- 000004 (Vector databases, agentic RAG, semantic plus deterministic search) covers the vector/semantic retrieval layer; 000005 and 000004 are designed to interoperate (graph for structure, vector for knowledge).
- 000002 (Prioritised search order for agentic knowledge retrieval) is the conceptual parent — establishes retrieval ordering principle that applies to all search/retrieval investigations including this one.

**Relevant governed documents:**
- PLAN-001 (agent-memory-system) specifies a Librarian retrieval router and explicitly defers vector embedding (phase-mem-15/16), with DuckDB VSS mentioned as the vector implementation path. Code-structure graph retrieval (this idea's focus) is not addressed.
- phase-mem-15 through phase-mem-19 in backlog.yaml are all deferred pending recorded retrieval failures. They focus on semantic/vector search, not code-structure graphs.
- PLAN-012 (terminology-system) treats retrieval as a solved problem and focuses on retrieval infrastructure, not new retrieval approaches.

**Critical context from ungoverned investigation:**
docs/00-working/ contains detailed analysis reports (gemini-knowledge-retrieval-report.md and related) that evaluate GitNexus, KuzuDB, and graph database alternatives. **Key finding: GitNexus is no longer adoptable.** KuzuDB (its embedded graph backend) was acquired by Apple and archived in October 2025, making the tool deprecated and unsafe for adoption. The reports recommend LadybugDB (KuzuDB community fork) as the closest successor if code-structure graph retrieval is pursued. This context post-dates idea 000005's creation and makes the specific tool proposal (GitNexus) stale, though the underlying need (graph-based code retrieval) remains valid.

The investigation already distinguishes code-structure graphs (for analyzing function/class/import relationships) from documentation/knowledge graphs (000044's domain) and both from semantic search (000004's domain). No plan is yet active in this space — the backlog work is deferred on evidence collection, and the working investigation is governance-ungoverned.

**No related plan, phase or ADR found.** The domain is active-but-ungoverned investigation, not yet a decision or plan. PLAN-017 touches graph identity (relationship edges for ideas/plans) but not code-structure or documentation graphs.

PROPOSED LINK: 000005 --relates_to--> 000044 (both about graph retrieval; 000005 focuses on code structure via GitNexus/KuzuDB, 000044 on documentation/knowledge databases)
PROPOSED LINK: 000005 --relates_to--> 000004 (both about knowledge retrieval mechanisms; graph (000005) and vector (000004) approaches are positioned as complementary, not competing)

author: agent-idea-triage
text:
Idea 000006 proposes auditing whether ID numbering schemes across the system have been chosen with a sufficient long-term horizon. This is explicitly cited in ADR-010, which explains that the ideas list identifiers were migrated from three digits to six digits before reaching a third entry, and references idea 000006 as the audit for whether other indexes in the system (project IDs, person IDs, commitment IDs, etc.) face the same risk of outgrowing their allocated width.

The database schema at sql/001_schema.sql uses VARCHAR for all ID columns without explicit length constraints, but ADR-010's motivation shows that schema definitions alone do not guarantee a width was chosen thoughtfully — three digits is valid DDL but insufficient in practice. No related plan, requirement or backlog phase explicitly addresses auditing ID capacity across the governed system.

Idea 000037 ("Split backlog.yaml into active and archive files before it clogs agent context") addresses capacity risk in a different artifact (the backlog file itself rather than ID width), and idea 000024 covers schema validation gaps, but neither overlaps with this idea's specific proposal to audit index widths.

author: agent-idea-triage
text:
Idea 000009 proposes an independent agent that reads a session's raw transcript—not the working agent's session record—to generate its own documentation, then runs adversarial review between the two accounts to surface blind spots. The idea explicitly composes with 000003 (mid-session notes skill) and relates to 000007 (idea-triage agent), both captured in the idea's own body.

Evidence for the concept is concrete: this session (SESS-2026-09-06-08) demonstrates the pattern. A third-party adversarial review with no conversational context returned 21 findings, three of which would have broken the next session—stronger evidence than the participant's own record alone would show. The idea proposes to extend this by reading raw transcript instead of relying on a participant's summary.

Related existing work: phase-ses-05 (session-close command) already implements third-party review of completion evidence, but it reviews a phase's acceptance conditions and deliverables *after* work is done, not the raw session transcript *as it unfolds*. The two address different review angles—one structural/post-hoc, one interpretive/parallel—and can coexist.

No related plan, requirement or phase documents transcript-as-independent-source analysis as a standing practice. The idea's design (deterministic extraction, diff-against-previous for incremental analysis) is unbuilt; its justification is concrete and grounded in this repository's own experience.

author: agent-idea-triage
text:
Idea 000012 proposes optimizing the test preflight in the `/backlog` command by skipping re-execution when the working tree is demonstrably clean and HEAD matches a commit already validated by CI.

The idea was explicitly identified as a finding during the design of the `/backlog` command (SESS-2026-09-06-08, "Eleventh amendment — the /backlog command", line 620-630). The session record documents it as an idea parked from the design work itself, noting that it is "free at 266 tests in under two seconds; not free later" and blocked on infrastructure that does not exist until `phase-priv-05`.

`phase-priv-05` is the final phase of PLAN-006 (Separate structure from content before the first remote push), which adds the first remote and enables CI gates. Once that phase completes, the preconditions for this optimization will exist: a remote with CI results that can be checked against current HEAD.

The idea's own analysis is sound: the value proposition (skipping redundant test runs once CI gates are in place) depends entirely on first pushing the code and establishing CI validation. The blocking dependency is explicit and correct. No other ideas directly overlap with this optimization proposal, and no plan currently addresses test-preflight skipping.

PROPOSED LINK: 000012 --relates_to--> depends on completion of `phase-priv-05` (part of PLAN-006, which gates this optimization's prerequisites)

author: agent-idea-triage
text:
Idea 000021 identifies a real gap between current governance and repository resilience during the pre-publish window. 

PLAN-006 (confidentiality sweep) gates the first remote push and manages the _private/ directory structure, but it is explicitly about separating structure from portfolio content before publishing, not about data durability. AGENTS.md forbids adding a remote until PLAN-006's phase-priv-05 completes, which means the entire repository history plus _private/ contents exist only on this machine's disk today. _private/'s permanent .gitignore exclusion also means even after the sweep lands and a remote is added, an off-machine copy would never include _private/ (the policy is intentional — real portfolio content must never leak to any remote by default).

The idea correctly observes that no governing document, ADR, or phase currently addresses what happens to the single local copy if the disk fails before the confidentiality sweep completes. REQ-002 defers a "durable storage and backup" question as an open item, but that one targets captured portfolio records (when they become real), not repository backup.

No related idea found by title overlap or links. No existing phase or document delivers the answer — whether the accepted posture is encrypted off-machine backup, a second local disk, or documented risk acceptance is an open design question.

Related governed documents:
- ADR-009 explicitly classifies people, commitments, and tasks as content (owner's real data), not structure, and notes PLAN-006 kept data-seeding as an open question rather than a substitute for real usage.
- PLAN-006 phase 3 mentions seeding "at least one person and one commitment with tasks," but specifies this is into the fictional public example set only, not addressing real usage barriers.
- phase-sig-03 (Accountability Ledger in doc-mini-systems) scopes "open external commitments joined to people," but its acceptance criterion is "Run synthetic people/commitment fixtures without creating real portfolio commitments" — confirming the team is still planning to work with test data only.

No requirements document or plan exists yet that addresses the tooling friction the idea identifies: ideas got tools/append_idea.py specifically because hand-editing JSON caused idea 000019 (corruption incident), yet no parallel writer exists for commitments (which require referencing project_id/people, making them non-trivial), or for people.

This idea directly precedes the infrastructure work that would enable real usage — the accountability ledger and other signals (phase-sig-03 through phase-sig-09) all depend on having data. The decision to build those signals before the data exists suggests the hypothesis is still unresolved.

No related idea found by title overlap.

text:
The HTML adversarial audit (ARCH-003, created 2026-09-05) directly addresses this gap. Finding M5 explicitly flags that "Existing CI compiles/builds TypeScript but does not exercise browser behavior" and recommends adding "representative navigation, retry, direct-link and responsive/block browser checks early enough to prevent regressions, rather than deferring all behavior testing to phase 10. TypeScript compilation alone is not rendering verification."

ARCH-003 also identifies M4 (responsive and accessible behavior has concrete gaps) which overlaps with the broader need for test infrastructure. The audit is cross-referenced in PLAN-005 and linked from multiple HTML phases, making it the active governance record for frontend verification strategy.

The related backlog phase "Restore the baseline Python lint gate" (docs/09-backlog/backlog.yaml) addresses linting for tools/ but does not cover TypeScript; idea 000026's question about which linter to standardize on remains open and separate from the Python gate.

The decision about whether to adopt test infrastructure now (cheap, on a two-file scaffold) or defer until HTML features begin remains unmade — ARCH-003 recommends early adoption to prevent regressions, but this finding itself does not assign an owner or phase to execute it. No promoted plan exists for TypeScript testing yet.

author: agent-idea-triage
text: Collision checking for declared deliverables paths exists in src/governance/backlog.py (ADR-003) for detecting overlaps *before* work starts; session-close command (PLAN-008, .claude/commands/session-close.md) runs third-party review of a phase's diff against its acceptance conditions. Manual deliverables containment checks are already performed during some session-close reviews (SESS-2026-09-08-04 validated that all changed files stayed within declared scope), but no mechanical validator currently enforces this post-completion. The idea proposes either adding containment validation to session-close's checklist or as an automated governance check. ADR-003 notes the collision detection rule ("Disjoint deliverables paths") and the need for rules to handle legitimate incidental touches (e.g., catalog.md). No other idea directly proposes this check. Not yet delivered.

author: agent-idea-triage
text:
Idea 000025 identifies a gap in the concurrent-agent protocol: AGENTS.md covers claiming a phase, working in a worktree, completing and handing off, and resolving merge collisions — but has no procedure for recovering when an agent claims a phase (marking it `status: active` and creating a worktree at `../d-system-worktrees/<phase-id>`), then stops mid-session without releasing the claim or completing the handoff (due to crash, timeout, context exhaustion, or session limit). The result is an indefinitely-locked phase, an orphaned worktree/branch, and blocked access for other agents.

ADR-003 covers the claim mechanism (backlog.yaml as lock table, `status: active` and `agent` field) and the handoff procedure (verification, session record, integration), but does not address stale or abandoned claims. The gap is real: the second agent mentioned in idea 000025's own body hit a session limit mid-research, illustrating the exact scenario.

Related infrastructure ideas (000029 "durable agent workflow run ledger with resumable steps", 000030 "always-on worker host and watchdog for supervised agent runs") address broader recovery capabilities but do not propose a specific procedure for claim recovery. Idea 000041 addresses a different collision scenario: preventing one agent from clobbering another's uncommitted work in the primary checkout, not recovering an abandoned claim.

The idea itself identifies three open design questions: what signals abandonment (staleness threshold, missing worktree directory, process status check), who may release another agent's claim (owner only, or any agent that can show evidence), and whether recovery is fully manual (documented procedure for owner to execute) or semi-automated (governance check that flags stale claims for review).

No existing plan, requirement, or phase currently covers claim recovery. PLAN-017 (idea lifecycle) and PLAN-016 (agent triage, phase-idea-02) touch idea-to-plan promotion but do not cover this operational scenario.

author: agent-idea-triage
text:
Idea 000030 proposes a supervised worker host and watchdog for agent runs—concurrency limits, quiet-hour deferral, heartbeat monitoring, and stale-run flagging for review. It is explicitly the third piece of a designed trilogy (after trigger gateway 000028 and run ledger 000029), with declared dependencies on both predecessors. The body acknowledges this intentional decomposition: "This only makes sense once the trigger gateway and run ledger ideas above exist; on its own it's a scheduling daemon with nothing to schedule."

No governed plan, requirement, or ADR yet exists for this infrastructure suite. ADR-003 touches autonomous-worker concurrency briefly but only in the Git context, not agent runs.

Related ideas 000028 and 000029 are named in the body but have no formal typed links yet. The trio forms a coherent feature set worth formalizing as a relationship graph.

PROPOSED LINK: 000030 --relates_to--> 000028 (part of supervised agent workflow infrastructure trilogy)
PROPOSED LINK: 000030 --relates_to--> 000029 (part of supervised agent workflow infrastructure trilogy)

author: agent-idea-triage
text:
Idea 000029 proposes a durable agent workflow run ledger enabling resumable multi-step agent execution — persisting run metadata, checkpoints, and idempotent delivery guarantees to recover from interruptions (crashes, timeouts, session limits). No existing plan, requirement, or ADR covers agent workflow durability; existing governance mentions agentic workflow triggering (PLAN-003) and agent concurrency coordination (PLAN-005, ADR-003) but not run persistence or resumable steps.

The idea was explicitly split from a combined "gateway + ledger" framing in research notes alongside 000028 (External trigger gateway) so the two can be evaluated independently — a relationship 000028's body confirms. Additionally, 000030 (Always-on worker host) is the third of three related infrastructure pieces for supervised agent runs, addressing deployment and watchdog concerns while 000029 handles durability. All three ideas emerged from the same research pass and are scoped to be decided independently.

No related plan, phase or document found covering run ledger or checkpoint resumption.

PROPOSED LINK: 000029 --relates_to--> 000028 (split from combined gateway+ledger concept, now separate ideas)
PROPOSED LINK: 000029 --relates_to--> 000030 (third piece of trilogy for supervised agent run infrastructure)

author: agent-idea-triage
text:
No existing plan, requirement, or ADR addresses runtime agent capability enforcement or approval-brokering for tool actions. PLAN-017 discusses approval gates for plan workflows and PLAN-001 covers memory deletion approval, but neither covers the mechanical enforcement boundary this idea proposes — denied capabilities enforced at the tool level with audit trails of attempted vs. succeeded actions.

The idea itself explicitly names two related initiatives: 000020 (MCP-mediated multi-agent coordination) whose "kill-switch" concept is complementary to this approval/capability boundary, and 000028 (external trigger gateway for unattended agent workflows), which would need this capability broker's enforcement to operate safely between chat sessions. Both relationships are mentioned in the body but not yet recorded as formal links.

author: agent-idea-triage
text:
Idea 000034 proposes a portfolio scenario simulator: isolated what-if projections that run signal computation against modified scenarios without touching source data or live databases. The idea explicitly states it depends on portfolio-signals system existing first (per PLAN-002-mini-systems-proposal.md, signal work is still planned, not implemented).

Related governed work:
- PLAN-002 (mini-systems-proposal) describes signal collection and portfolio-level synthesis, including a "Portfolio Digest" tier that rolls up signals to portfolio health analysis — the foundation this idea needs.
- The signals themselves would be the consumer this simulator creates (matching the idea's statement: "creates a concrete consumer for whatever the signal system eventually computes").

No other ideas overlap with this scenario-simulation capability. Idea 000033 (temporal projection explorer) explores historical portfolio changes; idea 000034 is about prospective what-if changes. No existing governed document delivers scenario simulation yet.

The idea is well-scoped and distinct from signal definition work — it's a new consumer and interaction layer, waiting on the signal layer to mature first.

author: agent-idea-triage
text:
Idea 000033 proposes a temporal projection explorer — a query layer and UI that exposes deterministic "as of" snapshots and diffs over ideas/plans/portfolio entities. It explicitly depends on PLAN-017 (idea/plan lifecycle architecture) and phase-idea-07's fold work.

Relevant governed material:
- PLAN-017.03 (event-contract-and-amendment-fold) already covers the amendment/fold mechanism and replay semantics that underpin temporal queries
- PLAN-016 and PLAN-017 discuss making history replayable ("past moment is reconstructible by replaying events"); this idea makes that capability user-facing
- PLAN-002 describes DuckDB views as a query tier already in use; temporal views would fit this pattern
- No existing plan yet covers exposing the time-axis via API/UI

Cross-checks with other ideas:
- Ideas 000008 (metrics/analysis), 000040 (deterministic search), and 000042 (ideas HTML dashboard) could potentially consume temporal data once this is built, but no overlap/duplication detected

Status: This is a well-positioned follow-on idea for after phase-idea-07 lands. The architecture is already designed (PLAN-017); this proposal is the first to surface the query interface itself as user-facing work.

author: agent-idea-triage
text:
Idea 000035 proposes automating cross-system contract enforcement from JSON Schema (Python models, TypeScript types, OpenAPI, fixtures) to prevent drift between backend, frontend, loader, and governance. This directly addresses the gap identified in idea 000024 ("Four entity schemas are validated in the pipeline with no DDL table, no data directory, and no CLAUDE.md mention"), which documents exactly this drift problem in production. PLAN-009 (capture build) already names the entities needing this workflow—task, interaction, decision, waiting_on, development_event—and PLAN-013 (tooling documentation) discusses drift enforcement as a governance tool that remains deferred. The idea is well-scoped as tooling rather than a new runtime system, with clear verification criteria; the open question of generic versus concrete-gap-only is the remaining design decision. Overlap with 000024 is substantial: 000024 surfaces the problem, 000035 proposes the solution mechanism.

PROPOSED LINK: 000035 --extends--> 000024 (proposes automation to fix the schema→DDL→model drift that 000024 identified)

author: agent-idea-triage
text:
Idea 000032 proposes a full dependency graph tracking sources and lineage for all generated outputs: memories, recommendations, reports, context packs, and metrics. It asks for bidirectional queryability ("why does this exist?" and "what needs reconsidering if this source changes?") plus persisted provenance through rebuilds.

Related governed documents exist but are narrower in scope:

- ADR-007 (Capture routing, provenance and the staging boundary) governs provenance for raw captured notes, not derived outputs.
- REQ-002 (Capture requirements) specifies confidence scoring and provenance fields per-record for captured items, but does not extend to generated reports/recommendations.
- PLAN-001 (Agent Memory System) lists "multi-model provenance" as an open question (how to resolve conflicts when different models write conflicting memories), but this is a narrow case within memory intake, not a system-wide lineage graph.
- backlog.yaml references provenance in multiple phases (memory editing, capture disposition, approval workflows) but all scoped to the capture/approval pipeline, not output traceability.

No existing requirement or plan covers the full end-to-end provenance system for derived artifacts (reports, rendered views, generated context) that 000032 proposes. The closest existing work (PLAN-001, REQ-002) handles memory intake and confidence at the source level, but nothing tracks what happened to that data downstream or links recommendations back to their evidence chain.

No related idea found.

author: agent-idea-triage
text: Idea 000037 proposes splitting backlog.yaml into active (non-terminal phases) and archive (completed/cancelled phases) to reduce context bloat when reading the raw file. The proposal is sound: GOV-002 (backlog protocol) establishes the preservation rule that prevents deletion, and the idea correctly notes that a location change is not a deletion and preserves the "preserve history" requirement. Related governed documents: GOV-002-backlog-protocol.md (the preservation rule and backlog protocol), PLAN-019-idea-priority-queue.md (backlog.yaml's next_up queue structure, though focused on ideas not phases), and PLAN-015-ephemeral-working-plans.md (which discusses archiving vs deletion for a different subsystem). The idea itself already notes tangential interaction with idea 000006 (index-width audit), which addresses numeric code ceilings rather than file size. No other ideas directly propose the same file-splitting change. No evidence found in governed documents that this work is already planned or in progress; the idea would require a requirement document and plan before implementation.

author: agent-idea-triage
text:
Idea 000036 proposes building a recommendation calibration system: persisting every recommendation produced (from signals, triage agents, advisory sources) alongside owner decisions (accept/defer/dismiss/revise), observed outcomes, and calibration metrics measuring recommendation effectiveness (precision, deferral rate, false-urgency rate, outcome lag).

Related existing work: PLAN-002 (mini-systems-proposal) establishes a signals/synthesis framework for computing derived views from portfolio data. The recommendation calibration loop is distinct — not a signal generator, but an audit trail and measurement system for evaluating whether advisory outputs helped. PLAN-016 (idea-record-system) covers idea event types; 000036 would need new event types for recommendation/decision/outcome tracking beyond idea scope. ADR-010 notes that 000036 was staged as ungoverned notes and deduplicated before recording.

Potential overlap: Idea 000032 (Evidence-backed provenance graph for memories, reports and recommendations) covers tracking sources and lineage for recommendations. Both ideas deal with recommendations as first-class tracked entities, but from different angles: 000032 focuses on provenance/source auditing ("why was this generated"), while 000036 focuses on outcome measurement ("did this actually help"). They would complement each other in a full recommendation management system.

No related plan, phase, or requirement document found that covers recommendation outcome tracking or calibration metrics.

PROPOSED LINK: 000036 --relates_to--> 000032 (both build recommendation-aware audit systems; 000032 covers provenance/sources while 000036 covers outcome calibration)

author: agent-idea-triage
text:
Idea 000038 asks for explicit formalization of the requirement-vs-plan distinction: when each is mandatory, what must/cannot go in requirements versus plans, whether unpaired plans need backfilling, and updated documentation (REQ/PLAN READMEs and AGENTS.md). Current state: AGENTS.md states the rule as a pair (requirement + plan before implementing) but practice has 18 plans against 4 requirements, with only one clean example (REQ-001/PLAN-005); nothing currently spells out the decision rule or contract between the two document types.

Related ideas: 000047 (Audit what makes a plan document qualitatively good: structure, style, tone, format) addresses the quality standards for plans themselves, complementing but not overlapping 000038's focus on the governance decision rule and distinction from requirements. Idea 000046 (An idea planner agent that turns a promoted idea into a governed plan) explicitly depends on 000047's rubric but would also benefit from 000038's formalization of when to draft a requirement versus a plan—however, 000046 does not name 000038 as a prerequisite.

Searched docs/01-plans/, docs/06-requirements/, docs/04-decisions/, docs/09-backlog/: found existing plan/requirement pairs (PLAN-005/REQ-001, PLAN-017/REQ-003, PLAN-018/REQ-004) but no explicit formalized decision rule, no written contract for what distinguishes the two document types, and no rubric for plan quality standards. OPS-001 requires acceptance criteria for plans; GOV-002 references phases mapped to plans; no other document currently addresses the gap 000038 identifies.

PROPOSED LINK: 000038 --relates_to--> 000047 (both establish standards for requirement and plan documents, 000038 on governance/distinction, 000047 on quality/rubric)

author: agent-idea-triage
text:
Idea 000042 proposes a generated HTML page combining open ideas and backlog phases in a single at-a-glance view, with ideas ranked by priority queue and phases by readiness/next_up status.

Related governed work:
- PLAN-003 (dynamic HTML generation) provides the general framework and templates/styles infrastructure this idea would build on
- PLAN-019 (idea priority queue) already delivers the ordered next_up list for ideas that would feed this view; implementation and documentation complete per backlog.yaml

Related ideas by title overlap (title-only inspection, not body verified):
- 000010 "Ideation dashboard" — broader dashboard concept that might encompass or extend what 000042 asks for
- 000039 "A priority queue for open ideas, mirroring backlog.yaml's next_up" — focuses on the priority-queue aspect that PLAN-019 has already implemented; potential duplication

The key unresolved design questions in 000042's body (generator location, static vs. dynamic serving, dependency-graph depth) align with the kinds of decisions PLAN-003's framework phases document. No existing governed document fully covers the combined ideas+backlog HTML view as specified.

author: agent-idea-triage
text: PLAN-001 (agent memory system) has already completed the core evaluation this idea proposes. The plan explicitly evaluates vector database options: recommends DuckDB VSS extension (no new infrastructure, fits the embedded-only stack) for Phase 2, lists specific embedding models (text-embedding-3-small, nomic-embed-text locally, with migration path to Qdrant for scale). It addresses the stated tradeoffs — ingestion via markdown/JSONL, embedding model selection with API vs. local fallbacks, scalability thresholds, and phase sequencing. The idea correctly identified that idea 000005 and 000020 do not evaluate tooling; PLAN-001 is where that evaluation lives. Overlaps with 000004 (vector databases and semantic retrieval), which should be checked for complementary scope.

author: agent-idea-triage
text:
Idea 000043 proposes building a queryable documentation database by projecting governed document metadata (front matter fields) into DuckDB, parallel to how _data/ projects into d_system.duckdb. This directly reverses ADR-001's explicit decision (ADR-001) to keep governance metadata out of DuckDB, treating it as development tooling rather than queryable business data.

Related foundational work exists: PLAN-005 establishes the front-matter schema and catalog generation; PLAN-013 covers tooling (validation, drift detection, catalog). PLAN-001 demonstrates the successful pattern of DuckDB as a retrieval layer (for memories, with tag filters, FTS, and VSS extension recommendations). No existing plan currently proposes a documentation database specifically.

The idea identifies companion explorations: idea 000044 is about graph database tooling for documentation/knowledge retrieval; idea 000045 is about vector database tooling for knowledge retrieval. These three ideas form the infrastructure layer for making documentation queryable — front matter schema and relational projection (000043), graph databases (000044), and vector embeddings (000045). Both companion ideas are mentioned in 000043's body but have not yet been formally linked.

This is infrastructure for the Librarian system envisioned in PLAN-001, not yet implemented. Open question in the idea: whether DuckDB-only is the right target or whether these should converge on a shared retrieval store (vector + graph).

PROPOSED LINK: 000043 --relates_to--> 000044 (companion ideas both exploring documentation/knowledge database infrastructure)
PROPOSED LINK: 000043 --relates_to--> 000045 (companion ideas both exploring documentation/knowledge database infrastructure)

author: agent-idea-triage
text:
This idea documents a concrete failure of the concurrent-agent protocol defined in ADR-003 (Worktree-isolated concurrent agents). The core issue: while a Claude session had uncommitted work in the primary checkout, a Gemini agent operating there ran git stash/pop operations that clobbered the other agent's changes without asking.

ADR-003 already mandates worktree isolation (agents work on separate branches at sibling paths like ../d-system-worktrees/<phase-id>) and claims via backlog.yaml commits on dev. The incident reveals two unaddressed gaps in the protocol:

1. **Primary checkout vulnerability:** Nothing prevents an agent from running destructive git operations (stash/pop, checkout, reset) against a shared primary checkout while a peer has uncommitted work there. ADR-003 permits primary-checkout operation only in specific contexts (docs/09-backlog/backlog.yaml notes "No governed document still forbids the primary checkout unconditionally"), but has no guard against concurrent misuse.

2. **Session code collision:** Session codes are allocated by inspection ("pick the next unused date-sequence number"), not atomically. Both concurrent sessions independently assigned SESS-2026-09-08-07, surfacing only after governance was rerun post-collision — too late for prevention.

The idea also surfaces an orphaned cleanup artifact (three leftover scripts in repo root) left from manual repair. Related to idea 000025 (abandoned claims — another concurrency-protocol failure mode where agents crash mid-session, leaving live claims and orphaned worktrees).

No existing plan or requirement document currently addresses prevention of destructive git operations during concurrent primary-checkout use or atomic session-code reservation.

PROPOSED LINK: 000041 --relates_to--> 000025 (both identify gaps in concurrent-agent protocol: 000041 addresses primary-checkout work clobbering and session-code collision; 000025 addresses abandoned claim cleanup)

author: agent-idea-triage
text:
Idea 000044 explores graph database tooling for documentation and knowledge retrieval. Strong overlaps exist with companion ideas in the same space:

**Explicit relationships in body:** 000044 directly references 000005 (Graph databases and GitNexus) as the code-structure graph counterpart, positioning itself as the documentation/knowledge side of the same design question.

**Related idea overlaps:**
- 000043 (Review documentation front matter and plan a documentation database for knowledge retrieval) approaches the documentation database problem from a front-matter-structured perspective, while 000044 explores the graph database implementation angle. Both aim to make the repository's cross-referenced documents queryable, just through different retrieval mechanisms.
- 000045 (Explore vector database tooling for a knowledge retrieval system) is the semantic search companion, exploring an alternative retrieval mechanism (vector embeddings) for the same documentation corpus. 000044's body explicitly names this as an open question: whether graph and vector approaches are complementary or competing.

**Governed documents:** PLAN-001 (agent memory system) covers The Librarian retrieval router and mentions vector search as one method, but does not address graph database exploration. No existing plan, requirement or backlog phase currently covers graph database evaluation for documentation systems.

000044 is properly scoped as a tooling exploration rather than implementation, with clear open questions about fit and positioning relative to both the code-structure graph use case and the vector-based retrieval alternatives.

PROPOSED LINK: 000044 --relates_to--> 000005 (Graph database exploration; explicitly positioned as the documentation counterpart to the code-structure graph)
PROPOSED LINK: 000044 --relates_to--> 000043 (Both target a queryable documentation database; 044 explores graph retrieval, 043 addresses structured approach)
PROPOSED LINK: 000044 --relates_to--> 000045 (Companion explorations of alternative retrieval mechanisms for the same knowledge corpus)

author: agent-idea-triage
text:
Idea 000049 identifies a real gap in governed documents: ADR-010 covers staging unformed ideas but explicitly stops at promotion, and PLAN-015 defines `_working/` as ephemeral task detail for existing phases—which is the wrong shape for a plan meant to become permanent. The gap surfaced concretely during triage of idea 000046 (an idea-planner agent), whose own body and triage findings both asked the same open question: does a drafted plan go straight into `docs/01-plans/` with a code allocated up front, or stage somewhere first?

This idea asks for a definition of the staging step (or an explicit decision that there isn't one). It should cover both the manual case (owner promoting an idea themselves) and the agentic case (a future planner agent doing the drafting).

Related: idea 000046 raised the open question this idea addresses. Idea 000047 (audit what makes a plan qualitatively good) is upstream infrastructure for both.

No related plan, requirement, or ADR beyond ADR-010 and PLAN-015 found that covers the mechanics of plan promotion.

author: agent-idea-triage
text:
Idea 000040 proposes formalizing a family of deterministic search algorithms for locating relevant documents across the system's expanding information surfaces (ideas, backlog, memories, decisions, governance docs, sessions). The proposal explicitly recognizes that this work complements rather than overlaps the vector/RAG research tracked in 000004 (Vector databases, agentic RAG, and semantic plus determinist) — 000040 focuses narrowly on the deterministic layer that should precede vector fallback in the retrieval stack.

Key finding: The deterministic retrieval architecture 000040 is asking to formalize is already partially described in PLAN-001 (agent-memory-system), which defines The Librarian agent and references "layers 1–4" of retrieval plus an "agentic retrieval loop." However, PLAN-001 asserts the layering order without designing the deterministic half — exactly the gap 000040 is asking research to fill. 000040's scope (structured query contracts, confidence signals for each algorithm, cross-algorithm result agreement) maps directly onto the missing design detail for those retrieval layers.

The idea explicitly calls out relationships to three other tracked initiatives: 000006 (Audit index widths before they run out) as part of the same volume-scaling trend; 000004 (Vector databases, agentic RAG) as the complementary semantic layer; and 000039 (A priority queue for open ideas, tied to PLAN-019) for which deterministic search provides upstream candidate-generation. Additionally, 000002 (Prioritised search order for agentic knowledge retrieval) addresses the ranking/ordering of results, which would follow deterministic search as a downstream step.

No related plan, phase or document fully addresses the deterministic search design question; PLAN-001 leaves it deferred. The idea's own unresolved questions — whether a single query contract serves all corpora, where the line between algorithm and DuckDB query lies, interactions with the priority-queue and triage systems — are appropriate for early research/survey before design.

PROPOSED LINK: 000040 --relates_to--> 000004 (deterministic search layer precedes the vector/RAG research already tracked)
PROPOSED LINK: 000040 --relates_to--> 000006 (both address search/system degradation as volume grows)
PROPOSED LINK: 000040 --relates_to--> 000039 (deterministic search generates candidates for priority queue to rank)

author: agent-idea-triage
text:
000014 investigates whether standing rules should be enforced by repository hooks rather than written procedures, and audits `.claude/settings.json` configuration.

This idea overlaps directly with PLAN-008 (session lifecycle protocols), which names 000014 explicitly as the venue for the enforcement question. PLAN-008 raises the same candidates (governance check, catalog staleness, no-remote gate) and the same open question about whether automation at the moment of action beats a documented step that can be skipped.

Pre-commit hook infrastructure is already under way: PLAN-006 (confidentiality sweep) and backlog phases reference wiring a checker into CI and pre-commit hooks.

Idea 000012 (Skip the test preflight when the tree is provably clean) raises the same architectural question — where automation belongs (hooks, tests, or written procedure) — and appears to be part of the same design conversation about enforcement boundaries.

PROPOSED LINK: 000014 --relates_to--> 000012 (both debate where enforcement should sit: hooks, tests, or written rules)

title: Idea management system
body:
Umbrella idea for the tooling that captures, triages, prioritizes, and surfaces parked ideas
as a coherent system rather than one-off scripts. Created to give ideas like 000007 (an agent
for triaging parked ideas) and 000010 (ideation dashboard) a shared parent to extend, since they
are both facets of the same idea-management capability rather than one extending the other.

title: Agent harness and guardrails
body:
Umbrella idea for the mechanisms that keep agent behavior inside guardrails: repository hooks,
settings.json enforcement, and test/preflight gating. Created to give ideas like 000012 (skip
the test preflight when the tree is provably clean) and 000014 (investigate hooks for the
repository and audit settings.json) a shared parent, since both are specific instances of
deciding where enforcement should live — hooks, tests, or written rules.

title: Schema-driven consistency across the pipeline
body:
Umbrella idea for treating JSON Schema as the single source of truth that DDL, Pydantic models,
test fixtures, and contracts should all derive from or be checked against, so drift between them
is caught mechanically instead of by inspection. Created to give ideas like 000024 (four entity
schemas validated in the pipeline with no DDL table, no data directory, and no CLAUDE.md mention)
and 000035 (contract compiler and mutation-driven fixture suite from JSON Schema) a shared parent,
since 000035 proposes automation whose root motivation is the same drift 000024 identified.

title: Allow ideas to link directly to plan/document IDs, not just other ideas
body:
Surfaced while triaging 000020 (MCP-mediated multi-agent coordination with a Librarian context
service): the finding wanted to record that 000020 relates to PLAN-001, but the idea log's
`linked` event only supports idea-to-idea edges (schemas/idea.schema.json's link `target` is
another idea id). There is no way to assert "this idea relates to this governed document" without
either finding a covering idea to link to instead, or leaving the relationship as prose in a
finding annotation where it isn't queryable.

Worth exploring whether `link` should accept a document code (PLAN-NNN, ADR-NNN, etc.) as an
alternate target shape, alongside idea-to-idea links, and what schema/rebuild changes that implies.

title: Observability and telemetry
body:
Umbrella idea for actually watching the system run: structured logging, metrics, and tracing
across the FastAPI backend, agent runs, and background tooling (rebuild_db, generation scripts).
Currently there is no consistent instrumentation — failures and slow paths are only visible if
someone happens to be looking at a terminal when they happen. Scope to work out: what to
instrument first (API request latency? agent run duration/outcome? DB rebuild timing?), where
telemetry data lives (a table, a log file, an external service), and how it differs from the
audit/provenance concerns in 000032.

title: A connection-builder agent for the full idea corpus
body:
An agent that maintains the relationship graph and tag assignments across every idea regardless
of status (open, triaged, promoted, discarded) — unlike 000007's triage agent, which is scoped to
open ideas only and never revisits ones that have already moved past that state. As the idea
corpus grows and 000004/000005/000043/000044/000045's graph and vector knowledge-retrieval work
lands, a stale or sparse relationship graph among ideas becomes a direct quality problem for that
retrieval layer, not just a bookkeeping gap.

Responsibilities:
- Build and maintain typed links (extends/supersedes/relates_to) between ideas across all
  statuses, including revisiting old ideas as new ones are captured that relate to them.
- Own tagging once 000018 ships — assigning and maintaining tags across the corpus, not just at
  capture time.
- Carry a triage-like surfacing role: proactively flag promising or high-value connections worth
  the owner's attention, not just mechanically record obvious ones.

Open questions: how it avoids clobbering or duplicating 000007's work on open ideas (does it run
after triage, or subsume it?), how it decides which candidate connections are worth surfacing
versus auto-recording, and what its relationship is to the idea-planner agent (000046) and the
idea scribe agent (000048).

title: Documentation governance
body:
Umbrella idea for keeping the docs/ tree itself correct, current, and internally consistent —
distinct from the governance check (src/governance) that already verifies structural integrity
(catalog entries, backlog phase references). This is about content quality and lifecycle: stale
documents that no longer reflect the systems they describe, front-matter consistency (see 000043),
and whether documents get retired/superseded cleanly when the thing they describe changes. Scope
to work out: what "governed" means beyond the existing catalog/governance mechanics, and whether
this overlaps with 000047's plan-quality audit closely enough to merge.

title: Testing strategy across the system
body:
Umbrella idea for a coherent testing approach across the whole system, not just the pieces that
already have coverage (test/ for the Python backend, 000001's HTML-generation fixtures). Currently
there is no test runner or lint gate for ts/ (000026), and no systematic approach ties schema
changes to fixture/contract regeneration (000035, under the 000052 schema-driven-consistency
umbrella). Scope to work out: what "tested" should mean per layer (backend routes, frontend
components, generation scripts, agent-facing tools like tools/append_idea.py), and whether a
single testing philosophy document is the right shape or whether it stays distributed per-system.

title: Version control and data redundancy
body:
Umbrella idea broader than git specifically: how the system's state (repository content, and
non-repository state like _private/'s gitignored portfolio data) is versioned and made recoverable
against loss. Git covers the tracked-repository half of this (see 000000's git-specific idea,
which extends this one); it does not cover redundancy for gitignored production data such as
_private/portfolio, which has no backup path at all today (000021) since the repo is deliberately
unpushed. Scope to work out: what "version controlled" should mean for non-git state, and whether
a backup/redundancy mechanism is a distinct system or an extension of git tooling.

title: Git tooling and practices
body:
The git-specific slice of 000058 (version control and data redundancy): branching/worktree
conventions, commit hygiene, hooks, and the concurrent-agent git-safety concerns already raised in
000025 and 000041. Extends 000058 rather than standing alone, since version control as a concept
covers non-git redundancy (e.g. _private/'s gitignored data) that git tooling itself can't solve.
